basis: Migne prints his own reference to Genesis 27:15 inside this answer, which asks 'Inter. 227. Quae sunt primogenita quae Esau vendidit Jacob fratri suo (vers. 31)?-- Resp.'. The extent is that reference and nothing wider.
date_basis: The dedicatory letter addresses Sigewulf, Alcuin's pupil and his successor at Tours, and says the questions are ones Sigewulf had put to him over a long acquaintance and are now gathered. Alcuin was abbot of Tours from 796 until his death in 804. The work is conventionally placed in the Tours years and near their beginning; the range records that and no more. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1851 printing, and it is not the seventh century the wiki header gives, which is a century out.
text: Inter. 227. Quae sunt primogenita quae Esau vendidit Jacob fratri suo (vers. 31)?-- Resp. Tradunt Hebraei omnes primogenitos fungi solitos officio sacerdotali [ Ms., sacerdotum] antequam Aaron in sacerdotem [ Ms., sacerdotium] eligeretur; et habuisse vestimenta sacerdotalia, quibus induti victimas Deo offerebant: et haec esse vestimenta 328 Esau, quibus Rebecca induit Jacob filium suum, quorum odore pater oblectatus benedictionis initium astruit (Gen. XXVII, 15).
